subject: Private deploy crypto handshake: proposed custodian pattern and data-transfer options
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medtech.co>

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — key custody and cross-border ops questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple items legal/ops want to lock down before we proceed with the pilot:

- We need clear language on who holds the master keystore and how emergency operator access is handled for VPC and on-prem options.
- Are there deployment patterns where Redwood never holds the unwrapped private keys (customer-only custody)? If so, what telemetry/metrics can we still provide for billing and health checks without seeing plaintext keys?
- Any subprocessors that would require cross-border data transfer or access to telemetry that could contain customer identifiers?

Can you share a short proposal for a custody pattern (options) and a list of subprocessors and their geographies? Legal would like a short timeline for any DPA addendums.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Infrastructure, MedTech Solutions

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medtech.co>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com; priyom_das@redwood.com; rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — key custody and cross-border ops questions

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answer up front: yes, we support a customer-only custody pattern for both VPC and on-prem private deployments; there are tradeoffs and operational controls to discuss. I've attached a short options doc that lays out three models and what telemetry we can safely expose in each.

Quick summary of the three models (see attachment for detail):
1) Customer-managed keystore (recommended): Customer holds master keys in their KMS/HSM. Redwood services operate on encrypted blobs; we never receive plaintext keys. We can emit aggregated billing metrics (token counts, latency percentiles) via hashed tenant ids.
2) Dual custody with split-encryption: Customer and Redwood each hold a key share used for wrapping. Requires a short-term key-release protocol for emergency breaks and more complex escrow processes.
3) Redwood-hosted keystore with strict operator controls: Redwood manages keys but with SOC2+ access procedures and limited operator break-glass. Least preferred for regulated PHI scenarios.

Subprocessors: Our core infra uses two partners that have visibility into telemetry: a Europe-based metrics provider (telemetry only, no request content) and a managed storage vendor in us-east. Both can be scoped in the DPA; no subprocessors will receive plaintext customer prompts or keys under model (1).

Next steps I propose:
- We (Redwood) send a concise custody proposal + DPA addendum draft by Mon Jun 28.
- Legal exchange for MedTech redlines the week of Jul 5.
- Pilot provisioning targeted for Jul 19, with a technical checklist for connectivity and KMS proofs-of-possession.

I'll loop in Laura and Priyom on the DPA/ops specifics below.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Security & Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: keystore-handshake-options.pdf

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Internal: MedTech — DPA addendum & subproc geography (notes)

Team —

Quick internal notes to prepare the draft Karthik promised:

- For model (1) customer-managed KMS: we must include proof-of-possession steps (RFC-style) before provisioning and a periodic attestation (30/90 days) to avoid accidental key leakage. Priyom, can you draft a minimal PoP checklist for on-prem HSMs and cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS)?
- Telemetry: provide hashed tenant id + sampling controls. We should be explicit that logs containing prompt snippets will be redacted and that we will provide an optional log-shipping lambda for customers who want to receive raw logs into their storage (avoids us having access).
- Subprocessors: list and country: metrics-provider (Germany), object-storage (US-East), CI vendor (US). Suggest we mark metrics-provider as 'telemetry-only' in the DPA and allow MedTech to request geo-restrictions.
- Emergency operator access: propose a 4-eyes approval flow, break-glass auditing, and time-limited key-release tokens that require customer-signed consent (DocuSign quick process). Rishi, note any infra constraints for implementing short-lived release tokens.

Priyom: draft the PoP checklist and the KMS binding language by EOD Wed Jun 30. Rishi: confirm feasibility of release-token flow by Thu Jul 1. Karthik: I'll assemble a one-page DPA addendum template to send to MedTech Monday.

Laura Bennett
Director, Trusted Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medtech.co>
Cc: legal@medtech.co; laura_bennett@redwood.com; priyom_das@redwood.com; rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed approach for keystore custody and DPA next steps (MedTech pilot)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled internal notes together. Attached is a short proposal and the proposed DPA addendum language — highlights below and proposed next steps so we can stay on a tight pilot cadence.

Summary of recommended approach (pilot):
- Custody model: Model (1) — Customer-managed keystore in MedTech's HSM or cloud KMS. Redwood will only receive wrapped keys and encrypted model state. No plaintext keys will be stored or processed by Redwood in the pilot.
- Telemetry & billing: We will emit aggregated, pseudonymized metrics (token counts, latency, errors) using a hashed tenant id. If you prefer, we can ship raw logs directly to your bucket so Redwood never persists prompt-level data.
- Emergency access: Implement short-lived key-release tokens: customer signs DocuSign authorization to lift the wrap for a 15-minute window. All events are logged and surfaced in the Console audit trail.
- Subprocessors: metrics-provider (Germany) — telemetry-only; object-storage (US-East) — encrypted blobs only; CI vendor (US) — not in production. We will include explicit geo-scoping language in the DPA addendum.

Timeline / next steps:
1) We attach the DPA addendum & custody proposal now — please review and return redlines by Jul 9.
2) Legal exchange Jul 12–16.
3) Technical PoP/ops checklist completed Jul 1 (done by our ops); pilot provisioning July 19.

Please let me know any redlines or if you want a short call (30 min) with our deployment engineers to walk the PoP steps and the DocuSign flow. Happy to set something up mid next week.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Product, Security & Deployments
Redwood Inference
